page.title: Financial Advisor
page.description: Run financial calculations for investments, loans, emergency funds, and net worth.

compound.title: Compound growth
compound.description: See how your money grows over time with compound interest — earnings that go on to earn more.
compound.infoBanner: Your money earns interest, and that interest also earns interest — creating exponential growth over years.
compound.emptyResults: Fill in your numbers and calculate to see growth results here.
compound.tipText: At {{rate}}%, the Rule of 72 says your money doubles in ~{{years}} years.

insight.excellent: Excellent growth! Your money grows {{multiplier}}x over {{years}} years — compounding is working strongly in your favor.
insight.good: Good growth — your investment more than doubles, with {{percent}}% coming from compound interest.
insight.moderate: Moderate growth. Consider increasing monthly contributions or a longer horizon.
insight.conservative: Conservative growth. A longer period or higher-return option would accelerate this.

retirement.title: Retirement projection
retirement.description: Estimates your retirement balance and monthly income using the "4% rule" — a guideline for safe 30-year withdrawals.
retirement.inflationHint: Average: 2–3%. Withdrawal rate uses the safe 4% rule.
retirement.emptyResults: Fill in your timeline and calculate to project your retirement.

adequacy.excellent: Your projected retirement income is excellent and should provide a comfortable lifestyle.
adequacy.good: Good retirement outlook. Consider increasing contributions to build more security.
adequacy.moderate: Moderate retirement income. You may want to increase savings or delay retirement.
adequacy.low: Your projected income is below typical needs. Consider significantly increasing contributions.

compare.title: Compare strategies
compare.description: See how contribution amounts and return rates affect your final balance, side by side.
compare.emptyResults: Set up your scenarios and compare to see which wins.
compare.differenceSummary: The difference between {{from}} and {{to}} is {{amount}} over {{years}} years.

selfSustaining.title: Self-sustaining portfolio
selfSustaining.description: Find the capital needed so monthly interest alone covers a fixed withdrawal — the balance no longer has to shrink to fund it.
selfSustaining.infoBanner: Once your balance is large enough that its monthly interest covers your withdrawal, you can draw that amount every month forever without depleting your capital.
selfSustaining.calculationError: Could not reach a self-sustaining balance with these inputs — try a higher return or contribution.
selfSustaining.emptyResults: Fill in your numbers and calculate to see your self-sustaining target.
selfSustaining.targetCapitalDetail: Generates {{interest}}/month in interest — enough to cover your {{withdrawal}} withdrawal
selfSustaining.sustainabilityCheckText: withdrawing {{withdrawal}}/month from {{capital}} for a year still leaves {{remaining}}.
selfSustaining.chartTitleSustainability: Balance during a year of withdrawals

amortization.title: Loan amortization
amortization.description: Your monthly payment and total interest over the life of the loan. Early on, most of your payment goes to interest; over time, more goes to principal.
amortization.emptyResults: Enter your loan details and calculate to see the payment breakdown.
amortization.summary: Over {{years}} years at {{rate}}%, you pay {{amount}} in interest — {{percent}}% on top of what you borrowed.

earlyPayoff.title: Early payoff
earlyPayoff.description: How extra monthly payments shrink your principal faster — and cut the interest that would otherwise accumulate.
earlyPayoff.emptyResults: Set an extra payment amount and calculate to see the savings.
earlyPayoff.tip: Extra payments go directly to principal, reducing future interest.

emergencyFund.title: Emergency fund
emergencyFund.description: Financial experts recommend 3–6 months of essential expenses saved for unexpected medical bills, repairs, or job loss.

reasons.threeMonthsText: Minimum safety net for stable jobs

emergencyFund.analyzeIntro: We'll analyze your actual spending over the last 6 months to calculate a personalized recommendation.
emergencyFund.emptyResults: Run the analysis to see your emergency fund recommendation.
emergencyFund.notEnoughDataFallback: We need more expense transactions to calculate a recommendation.
emergencyFund.notEnoughDataHelp: To calculate your emergency fund needs, make sure you have:

notEnoughDataChecklist.expenses: Expense transactions recorded in your accounts
notEnoughDataChecklist.history: At least a few weeks of spending data

emergencyFund.coverageDetail: {{assets}} in liquid assets · monthly expenses average {{expenses}}
emergencyFund.goalReached: Congratulations! You've reached your recommended emergency fund target.

status.excellent: You have a robust emergency fund that can cover extended periods without income. Great job!
status.good: Your emergency fund is solid. Consider continuing to build toward 6+ months for extra security.
status.fair: Your emergency fund is below recommended levels. Prioritize building this up before other investments.
status.critical: Your emergency fund is critically low. Focus on saving at least 1–2 months of expenses immediately.

netWorthTool.title: Net worth tracker
netWorthTool.description: Net worth = total assets − total liabilities. A positive net worth means your assets exceed your debts.
netWorthTool.infoBanner: Assets: cash, investments, property, vehicles. Liabilities: loans, credit cards, mortgages.
netWorthTool.emptyResults: Pick a view above to see your net worth.

history.infoBanner: Estimated net worth over the past 12 months, based on your transaction history.
history.chartHint: The line is your net worth; the bars under it are what each month added or took away.

projection.infoBanner: This projection assumes your current savings rate continues.
projection.chartHint: Dashed and shaded because it is arithmetic on your current savings rate, not a record of anything.

health.excellent: Excellent! Your debt-to-asset ratio is very healthy.
health.good: Good financial position with manageable debt levels.
health.moderate: Moderate debt levels. Consider focusing on debt reduction.
health.high: High debt ratio. Prioritize paying down liabilities.

aiAdvisor.unavailableReason: AI chat is not configured on this server. Set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY on the backend to turn it on.

chat.heading: Ask your money anything.
chat.subheading: The advisor reads your real transactions, balances, budgets, recurring bills and debts as it answers — and can email you a copy of anything it works out.
chat.composerHint: Enter to send, Shift + Enter for a new line.
chat.unreachableError: The advisor could not be reached ({{status}}).
chat.emptyResponseError: The advisor returned an empty response.
chat.streamError: Something went wrong reaching the advisor.

findLeak.title: Find the leak
prompts: What are my top 3 expense categories this month?
Which subscriptions am I paying for that I barely use?

checkPlan.title: Check the plan
prompts: Am I on track with my budgets?
Which recurring expenses hit in the next 7 days?

getOutOfDebt.title: Get out of debt
prompts: How much total debt do I have, and what should I pay off first?
If I put an extra 200 a month at my debts, when am I clear?

portfolioHealth.title: Check the portfolio
prompts: Am I too concentrated in any one holding?
How risky is my portfolio compared to the market?

investDecision.title: Decide where it goes
prompts: How much can I realistically invest each month?
Should I add to my biggest holding or buy a broad index fund?
Would I be better off paying down my debt than investing?

labels.getPortfolioAllocation: Checking how your portfolio is spread
labels.getInvestableSurplus: Working out what you can invest
labels.compareInvestVsPayoff: Comparing investing against paying it off

investorProfile.title: Investor profile
investorProfile.description: Who the AI advisor thinks you are. It reads this before every answer, and checks any suggestion against your limits. Leave a field blank if you'd rather it asked.
investorProfile.notSetYet: Nothing set yet. Until you fill this in, the advisor will ask before giving allocation advice rather than assuming.

fields.liquidityNeedsMonths: Months of expenses to keep liquid
fields.notes: Anything else the advisor should know

hints.horizonYears: How long before you'd need this money.
hints.maxSinglePosition: The advisor will flag any suggestion that pushes a holding past this.
hints.targetAllocation: The split you're aiming for. Percentages, adding up to about 100.
hints.notes: e.g. "I already have a workplace pension" or "I don't want to hold individual stocks"

history.title: Change history
history.description: Every change, including the ones the advisor made for you. Undo restores the previous value.
